_readme: MONEY-1357 — the DATA-level backstop under the liveness gauge.
The two are not redundant, and the difference is worth stating: rt.health_ok
is the service's own OPINION of itself, and this counts what it actually
PRODUCED. A holder that is connected, leader, and receiving frames it cannot
turn into bars reports healthy and writes nothing — `decideHealth` watches the
socket, not the aggregator. Only this row sees that.
`default_zero()` is what makes it an absence check rather than a second
no-data monitor: a window with no points renders as a real 0 and the
threshold evaluates, instead of the series going grey.
_window_rationale: 96h, and the arithmetic is the point rather than caution.
The feed is the 24x5 consolidated venue: 04:00-20:00 ET, Monday to Friday. So
the longest legitimate gap is Friday 20:00 ET to Monday 04:00 ET = 56 hours,
and that is the number a window has to clear. 96h clears it with room for a
US market holiday on either side of a weekend — Thanksgiving Thursday plus
Friday's early close, or a Monday holiday, both of which extend the gap past
A 36h window would sit below threshold every single weekend, which is
bhavcopy-sync's mistake (MONEY-1238) one timezone further out, and is how a
monitor somebody depends on gets muted.
name: [{{env}}] tiingo-realtime — no minute bars closed in 96h
message:
tiingo-realtime has closed NO minute bars in 96 hours.

This is the data-level backstop under the liveness gauge, and it catches the case that one cannot: a holder that is connected, leader and receiving frames, but producing no bars. `rt.health_ok` watches the SOCKET; this watches the OUTPUT.

96h clears the real maximum gap — the feed is 04:00-20:00 ET Mon-Fri, so Friday close to Monday open is 56 hours, plus room for a US holiday.

If `rt.health_ok` is fine and this fired, look at the aggregator rather than the connection: `rt.frames_received` still climbing with `rt.bars_closed` flat, or `rt.refused_no_listing` rising (symbols with no resolvable US listing), or `rt.refused_mixed_source` (a day already holding EOD bars, which realtime must not overwrite).

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: FALSE, and 4320 — corrected. This read `true` / 17280, which is FOUR TIMES
Datadog's measured ceiling of 4320 minutes (72h). The clamp that enforces
that ceiling, `window_limits`, lives in apply-monitors.sh; THIS template is
rendered by apply-service-monitors.sh, which has no clamp — so nothing
between the literal and the API would have caught it.
It was masked, not harmless. The `metric-rt-bars` preflight refuses this row
while `rt.bars_closed` has no points, so the POST never happened. The day the
series gets points — exactly when this monitor starts meaning something — the
POST is refused 400 "No data timeframe must be <= 4320", the row lands in
FAILED, and the script exits 1 on every run after that.
The value is 4320 because that is the ceiling; `notify_no_data` is FALSE
because of the rule `window_limits` applies to every other monitor in this
directory. A no-data alarm means something only when its timeframe EXCEEDS
the job's legitimate maximum gap. This window is 96h precisely because the
gap can pass 72h (see `_window_rationale`: a US holiday either side of a
weekend), so a 72h no-data alarm would fire on a healthy holiday weekend —
which is how bhavcopy-sync's monitor got muted (MONEY-1238).
Nothing is lost by turning it off. default_zero() is the MECHANISM here: a
window with no points renders as a real 0 and the threshold evaluates. The
one case default_zero cannot cover — a tag combination that has NEVER
existed, so there is no series to fill — is covered at apply time instead, by
the `metric-rt-bars` preflight, which refuses the row outright when
`stockbook.rt.bars_closed` has no points.
